Charles L. Christ | Charles Louis Christ (March 12, 1916 – June 29, 1980) was an American scientist, geochemist and mineralogist.  He received his Bachelor's, Master's and Doctoral degrees from the Johns Hopkins University, completing his Ph.D. in 1940.  After receiving his degree, he worked for the General Electric Company as a research chemist in Pittsfield, Massachusetts.  In September, 1941 he returned to academia as an instructor at Wesleyan University. From 1942–1945 he returned to Hopkins as an instructor and Associate Director of their C.Y. War Research Laboratory.  The Laboratory was responsible for developing a super-conducting bolometer for the detection of infrared radiation.  From 1946–1949 he was group leader for X-ray crystallography at the American Cyanamid Company in Stamford, Connecticut.
